description: Patient burden taxonomy — the cross-cutting axis applied to clusters (and, in future, segments) regardless of indication or source. Categories are inspired by the treatment-burden literature (Eton 2012, May 2014, Tran 2015) and patient-reported outcome frameworks; subcategories refine within each top-level. Tree structure: parent_id = null at the top level. This v1 is a defensible starting point for editorial review — refine the granularity and rename freely; FKs are the ids, not the labels.
references: Eton DT et al. (2012). Building a measurement framework of burden of treatment in complex patients with chronic conditions.
May CR et al. (2014). Rethinking the patient: using Burden of Treatment Theory to understand the changing dynamics of illness.
Tran VT et al. (2015). Adaptation and validation of the Treatment Burden Questionnaire (TBQ) in English using an internet platform.

items.label: Financial burden
items.description: Direct and indirect monetary cost of disease and treatment — out-of-pocket spend, insurance navigation, lost income.

items.label: Out-of-pocket cost
items.description: Co-pays, deductibles, uncovered medications and procedures.

items.label: Insurance / coverage navigation
items.description: Prior authorization, claims, appeals, coverage gaps, and benefit-design friction.

items.label: Lost income / employment impact
items.description: Time off work, reduced productivity, job loss, or career impact from disease or treatment.

items.label: Physical burden
items.description: Bodily experience of the disease and its treatment — symptoms, side effects, appearance changes.

items.label: Disease symptoms
items.description: Symptoms attributable to the disease itself (pain, fatigue, swelling, flares).

items.label: Treatment side effects
items.description: Adverse effects from medications, procedures, or therapy.

items.label: Appearance changes
items.description: Visible changes from disease or treatment (weight, hair, skin, rashes) and their experiential impact.

items.label: Emotional / psychological burden
items.description: Affective and mental-health load of living with the disease and its trajectory.

items.label: Fear / anxiety
items.description: Worry about progression, treatment risks, recurrence, or future.

items.label: Grief / loss
items.description: Mourning lost capacities, identity, or imagined futures.

items.label: Isolation
items.description: Feeling alone with the illness; lack of understanding from others.

items.label: Uncertainty
items.description: Not knowing what's coming, conflicting information, ambiguous prognosis.

items.label: Treatment regimen burden
items.description: Day-to-day workload of executing a treatment plan — taking medications, monitoring, attending visits.

items.label: Adherence / pill burden
items.description: Number, frequency, and complexity of medications; difficulty sticking to schedule.

items.label: Self-monitoring effort
items.description: Home labs, blood pressure, glucose, symptom logs, weight, device readings.

items.label: Appointments / visits
items.description: Frequency and density of clinic visits, infusions, procedures.

items.label: Information / decisional burden
items.description: Cognitive load of understanding the disease and treatment choices.

items.label: Knowledge gaps
items.description: Not knowing what a label means, what a trial is, or what to expect.

items.label: Decision complexity
items.description: Hard tradeoffs across treatment options with imperfect information.

items.label: Care navigation
items.description: Coordinating across specialists, systems, and resources.

items.label: Social / relational burden
items.description: Impact of disease and treatment on relationships, identity, and social participation.

items.label: Stigma
items.description: External or internalized judgment tied to the condition or its visible effects.

items.label: Relationships
items.description: Strain on partners, family, friendships; caregiver dynamics.

items.label: Disclosure
items.description: Deciding when and how to tell others about the condition.

items.label: Time / logistical burden
items.description: Time-cost and operational friction of life-with-disease.

items.label: Travel / transport
items.description: Distance to clinic, transit, parking, accommodations.

items.label: Scheduling
items.description: Calendar friction across appointments, work, family obligations.

items.label: Caregiver dependence
items.description: Reliance on others for transport, supervision, or daily activities.

items.label: Quality of life
items.description: Felt impact on function, independence, and the experience of normalcy.

items.label: Functional limitations
items.description: Ability to do daily activities, work, exercise, hobbies.

items.label: Loss of independence
items.description: Dependence on others; reduced autonomy in daily life.

items.label: Loss of normalcy
items.description: Feeling that life-with-disease is not the life one had or expected.
